analysis:
Integration of all 39 units found no supported finding. The PR adds KV-pool and allocator-cache reclaim, and nothing in the supplied evidence touches the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), key custody (A-002, A-003), attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), E2E encryption, or the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041: HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, DBK3 crypto, cacheSalt scoping).

What changed:
- Docs describe parked free 64 MiB KV segments per pool, up to min(2 GiB, grant/8). They sit outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. They are reinstalled at the next admission of the same size class. They are dropped on a refused charge, on memory pressure, at load gates, and after 30 s idle. Rollbacks are DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0.
- Code adds releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad to the ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift, StandaloneServer.swift and StartupPreloader load gates. It adds a reclaim hook when headroom is short and a windowed idle sweep (KVPoolReclaimer, WholeMacServiceBudget.performIfIdle). It adds ProcessMemoryLedger.capacityShortfall and a refusal signal for MiMo media and engine charges (MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation, MiMoV26NativeLoadTransaction.swift:963-964 and 1074, EngineProcessMemoryOwner).
- LaunchAgent.swift adds the three env keys to a fixed allowlist. The values are operator-local, and the operator is already ADV-001 with local control. No arbitrary environment injection is possible.
- The reclaim paths keep the nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed and isReclaimAllowed guards. A refused charge still throws, so admission fails closed. The refusal signal carries only a byte count.
- The test files add coverage only.

Residual questions that I could not verify, because these files were not supplied (PagedKVSegments.swift, EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, the CBv2RetainedKVSegments and releaseRetainedKVSegments implementations):
1. T-028: whether a retained segment reinstalled for a different request or account is overwritten or length-bounded so stale KV is never readable. New segments are documented as zero-fill-on-demand, and nothing says reinstalled ones are re-zeroed. The exposure is in-process, and ADV-001 already has memory access (T-014).
2. Whether the uncharged retained bytes (up to 2 GiB) stay correctly accounted as reclaimable, so over-admission is avoided (T-029, T-010).
3. Whether performIfIdle holds the admission lock across a blocking GPU clearCache, which would be an availability concern.
4. Whether the refusal-triggered reclaim is rate-limited against a consumer who induces repeated refusals.

T-028 may deserve a note about retained segments once the implementation is confirmed.
